definitions.explanation: The pursuit of or devotion to beauty and sensuous pleasure, especially in art and literature. In modern Japanese pop culture, also refers to a genre featuring beautiful, often romantic depictions of male characters.

examples.japanese: {耽美|たんび}{的|てき}な{世界観|せかいかん}。
{耽美|たんび}{主義|しゅぎ}の{文学|ぶんがく}は{美|うつく}しさを{最|もっと}も{重要|じゅうよう}な{価値|かち}とする。
examples.english: Aestheticist literature regards beauty as the most important value.

examples.japanese: {谷崎|たにざき}{潤一郎|じゅんいちろう}は{日本|にほん}の{耽美|たんび}{派|は}を{代表|だいひょう}する{作家|さっか}として{知|し}られている。
examples.english: Tanizaki Jun'ichiro is known as a leading writer of the Japanese aestheticist school.

notes: In literary criticism, {耽美|たんび}{主義|しゅぎ} (aestheticism) refers to the art-for-art's-sake movement. Japanese writers associated with this school include {谷崎|たにざき}{潤一郎|じゅんいちろう} and {永井|ながい}{荷風|かふう}. In modern pop culture, {耽美|たんび} is used as a genre label for manga, anime, and fiction featuring idealized, often androgynous male characters and romantic relationships between men (overlapping with BL/ボーイズラブ). Common compounds: {耽美|たんび}{主義|しゅぎ} (aestheticism), {耽美|たんび}{的|てき} (aesthetic), {耽美|たんび}{派|は} (aestheticist school).
